bib.title: Recurrent Memory Transformer
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2022 (36th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)

question: Can a Transformer get long-term memory and segment-level recurrence just by adding memory tokens to input and output, with no architecture change?
hypothesis: Dedicated memory tokens with recurrence store global information more compactly than Transformer-XL's mixed hidden-state cache, so smaller memory suffices on long-sequence tasks.
contributions: Augment Transformer with token-based memory storage and segment-level recurrence.
Evaluate vs Transformer and Transformer-XL on copy, reverse, associative retrieval, quadratic equations and language modeling; RMT beats Tr-XL on sequence tasks and matches it on LM with less memory.
Tr-XL cache can be combined with RMT for better LM performance.
Analysis of learned memory read/write attention patterns.

method.summary: m real-valued [mem] tokens are put at the start (read) and end (write) of each segment; write-token outputs become the next segment's read tokens, trained with BPTT across segments. Built on the Transformer-XL code base; also added to pretrained BERT/RoBERTa/DeBERTa/T5 for classification.
method.task: long-sequence processing: algorithmic tasks, language modeling, long text classification

datasets.name: Copy / Reverse (synthetic)
datasets.size: train 100000, valid 5000, test 10000 (for copy 24, reverse 24, assoc. retrieval); sequence sizes 24, 40, 120, 240, 360
datasets.preprocessing: character-level tokenization; loss only on target segments

datasets.name: Associative retrieval
datasets.source: generator code from Ba et al. 2016

datasets.name: Quadratic equations (synthetic)
datasets.source: generated; roots uniformly sampled from -100 to 100, coefficients scaled by 1..10, 20 percent no real roots
datasets.preprocessing: char-level, each step padded to 30 tokens

datasets.name: WikiText-103
datasets.preprocessing: context 150 tokens, or segment 50 for long-recurrence runs

datasets.name: enwik8
datasets.size: 10^8 first bytes of Wikipedia XML; vocab 204 characters

datasets.name: Hyperpartisan news
datasets.split: train/valid/test as in Beltagy et al. 2020
datasets.preprocessing: 500 input tokens per segment; up to 4 segments (about 2000 tokens)

models.name: RMT (WikiText-103)
models.architecture: Transformer-XL code base, decoder-only, memory tokens

models.name: RMT + BERT-base / RoBERTa-base / DeBERTa-v3-base / T5-base
models.architecture: pretrained HF model + 10 memory tokens + recurrence

models.name: Transformer-XL
models.architecture: segment recurrence with stop-gradient cache of m states per layer

models.name: Baseline Transformer (Tr-XL memory 0) and Memory Transformer (MemTr)
models.architecture: decoder-only; MemTr has memory tokens without recurrence

training.objective: language modeling / target-sequence cross entropy (loss only on target segments for algorithmic tasks); classification fine-tune for Hyperpartisan; auxiliary memory loss for Tr-XL+RMT
training.lr: 0.00025 (LM, linear schedule); 1e-4 constant with reduce-on-plateau factor 0.5 (copy, reverse, quadratic)
training.regularisation: auxiliary loss on memory tokens, multiplier 0.01, for Tr-XL+RMT (a fixed special token predicted from memory)
training.hardware: 1080 Ti (seq 24 tasks), V100 x1-3 (longer copy/reverse), 2x A100 80GB (LM)
training.wall_clock: LM: 10 to 30 hours; seq-24 tasks 1 hour to 2-3 days; longer copy/reverse 1 hour to 3-4 days; quadratic 1-2 days

other.BPTT unroll: 0 to 4 segments; instability and out-of-memory for larger memory with deeper unroll

inference.samples: std reported on key experiments; number of seeds not stated

eval.protocol: mean ± std over runs (count not stated)

availability.data: synthetic generators in code; WikiText-103, enwik8 public

results.claim: RMT with 10 memory vectors (BPTT-3) nearly matches Tr-XL with 25 cached states per layer on WikiText-103 and sits close to Tr-XL memory 75, at segment length 150.
results.setup: WikiText-103, 16-layer, segment 150, RMT BPTT-3 memory 10; Tr-XL mem 25 = 25.57, mem 75 = 24.68, baseline 29.95
results.table: Table 2, row RMT BPTT-3 (memory 10, segment 150), column PPL±STD

results.claim: RMT with 1 memory vector at segment length 50 is about as good as Tr-XL with memory 10.
results.setup: WikiText-103, segment 50, RMT BPTT-1 memory 1; Tr-XL memory 10 = 28.98
results.table: Table 2, row RMT BPTT-1 (memory 1, segment 50), column PPL±STD

results.claim: Combining Tr-XL cache (150) with 10 RMT memory tokens gives the best WikiText-103 result, slightly under the Tr-XL paper's 24.0.
results.setup: WikiText-103, segment 150, Tr-XL+RMT 150+10, 2x steps (400k) per Table 5; auxiliary memory loss weight 0.01
results.note: Table 2 row has no '2X steps' tag; Table 5 shows 24,25 / 24,30 for non-2x variants and 23,99 for BPTT-3 2X STEPS. Table 5 uses decimal commas for these rows.
results.table: Table 2, row TR-XL + RMT (150+10), column PPL±STD

results.claim: Transformer-XL with 40 cached states per layer matches RMT with memory size 5 on enwik8.
results.setup: enwik8, 12-layer, segment 128; RMT BPTT-1 mem 5 = 1.241; Tr-XL mem 40 = 1.230
results.table: Table 4, row RMT BPTT-1 (memory 5, segment 128), column BPC±STD

results.claim: Deeper BPTT unrolling improves RMT: memory 10, segment 50, perplexity falls from BPTT-0 to BPTT-4.
results.setup: WikiText-103, segment 50, memory 10, RMT BPTT-4; BPTT-0 = 30.69
results.table: Table 5, row RMT BPTT-4 (memory 10, segment 50), column PPL±STD

results.claim: On quadratic equations (180 tokens, 6 segments, memory 30) RMT solves the task and Tr-XL does not.
results.setup: Algorithmic, 6 segments; RMT 0.99±0.002, Tr-XL 0.93±0.02, unsegmented baseline 0.99±0.01

results.claim: RMT on RoBERTa-base reaches the best Hyperpartisan F1 in Table 3, above Longformer and Big Bird with 4096 inputs.
results.setup: Hyperpartisan news, RoBERTa-base augmented with 10 memory tokens, 512 per segment, 4 segments; Longformer 94.80, Big Bird 92.20, Ernie-Doc-large 96.60
results.table: Table 3, row RMT ROBERTA-BASE [512], column 4 segments

results.claim: Copy task: RMT solves it perfectly up to 9 segments at fixed length 360 while Tr-XL falls to the no-memory baseline.
results.setup: Copy, source+target 360 tokens, memory = segment length; read from Fig 4a
results.quote:
With the number of segments up to 6 mean accuracy of Transformer-XL drops by up to 0.2 points, and with 9 segments plunges
close to the baseline without memory.

results.claim: RMT compresses a 12-token copy over 6 segments into 6 memory tokens; Tr-XL with memory 6 on reverse (4 segments) gets 0.8 against RMT 1.
results.quote:
giving average
accuracy of 0.8 on the target task. Despite having the same memory size, RMT manages to compress
the whole segment in memory tokens (Appendix B Figure 9(a)) and achieve mean accuracy 1.

results.claim: Authors state RMT matches Tr-XL quality with up to 10 times smaller memory.
results.setup: Language modeling, WikiText-103 and enwik8; note Tr-XL memory is per layer (10 x 16 vectors) while RMT is memory_size vectors
results.quote: shows quality metrics similar to Transformer-XL but for up to 10 times smaller memory size

limits: Authors concede training instabilities and GPU RAM/OOM issues for larger memory with deeper BPTT unroll (Sec 5, checklist 1b).
Memory sizes are not like-for-like: Tr-XL memory is states of every layer, RMT memory is vectors at the input only.
Experiments are small (16-layer, 410-hidden LM; synthetic tasks); batch size, warmup, dropout, seeds not stated.
Associative retrieval at 5 segments: RMT slightly drops and Tr-XL rises above.
Information must fit a fixed memory over more steps: harder as segments shrink.
RMT matches but does not beat Tr-XL on language modeling at equal training; best result needs the combination.

terms.definition: The starting group of memory tokens lets sequence tokens attend to previous-segment memory; the ending group attends to all current tokens and holds the updated memory passed on.
